chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, said:
"The third call to prayer (Adhan) on Friday is an innovation."

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqṭīnī, from Zakariyya al-Mu'min, from Ibn Najiyah, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Sayyabah, from Najiyah, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

"When you have prayed the 'Asr prayer on Friday, say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, the Successors who are pleased, with the best of Your blessings, and bestow Your blessings upon them with the best of Your blessings, and peace be upon them and upon their souls and bodies, and the mercy of God and His blessings."

He said: "Whoever says it after the 'Asr prayer, God will record for him one hundred thousand good deeds, erase from him one hundred thousand bad deeds, fulfill for him one hundred thousand needs, and raise him by it one hundred thousand degrees."
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And know that the narration comes to his saying 'and the Friday [prayer] is dropped'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the third Adhan on Friday and what is the recommended supplication after Asr prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights two distinct Friday practices: the first narration critiques the third Adhan as a later innovation (*bid'ah*), reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the evolution of communal rituals, while the second emphasizes the spiritual potency of specific Salawat recited after 'Asr. The detailed rewards—such as the cancellation of 100,000 sins and the fulfillment of needs—underscore the day's significance in Shia piety, linking ritual action with divine grace and intercession through the Ahl al-Bayt.
